dangerous_cpts.main_problem: The same xray parameter was activated in both failure scenarios and in no success scenarios. It lies directly on the disease-to-finding path and can independently distort diagnosis because an abnormal X-ray is strong evidence for tuberculosis or lung cancer in this network. The activated parameter predicts xray=yes when either=yes with probability 0.8, so if failures repeatedly involve this path, the strength of this likelihood is a plausible contributor rather than merely a downstream consequence.

suspicious_parameters.justification: This parameter strongly favors abnormal X-ray whenever either disease is present. Given repeated failure-only activation, the evidential impact from either to xray may be overstated, causing the network to overcommit to disease-consistent explanations.

dangerous_cpts.main_problem: The same dysp parameter was activated in both failure scenarios and in no success scenarios. Dyspnea is a major symptom node with two parents, so its CPT has substantial independent influence on posterior diagnosis. The activated entry corresponds to bronc=yes and either=yes, where dysp=yes is assigned very strongly (0.9). Repeated failures along this configuration suggest the symptom likelihood may be too strong and may be reinforcing incorrect disease explanations.

suspicious_parameters.justification: This entry makes dyspnea almost certain when both bronchitis and either disease are present. Because dyspnea is nonspecific in the medical domain, such a strong probability can overweight this symptom and repeatedly support wrong predictions.

overall_summary: The strongest plausible refinement candidates are xray and dysp. Both have failure-only activation across the repeated failure pattern and both are probabilistic medical evidence nodes whose likelihood strengths can independently bias diagnosis. The candidate either parameter is not included because either is a deterministic OR node; its suspicious activation is more naturally explained by upstream disease assignments than by an independently flawed CPT.
